jobs.title: Senior Developer Advocate, AI Content & Community
Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning
Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning

reading.body:
Five open developer relations and education roles in AI, posted between August 14 and October 2, 2026, at Lambda, SambaNova, Databricks, and the U.S. Air Force Academy.

The pattern is that the demand is for people who teach, not people who build. Four of the five are developer advocate or developer relations titles at chip and platform companies, and the fifth is a faculty post teaching STEM and artificial intelligence. Databricks is hiring the same role twice, in Seattle and San Francisco, which suggests a team being staffed rather than a single seat being filled.

For AI specifically, this is the layer that sits between compute and the people who use it. Lambda and SambaNova sell compute capacity, and developer advocates are how that capacity gets adopted by engineers who have to write against it. The Air Force Academy posting is the only one with a published salary, $85,423 to $168,838, and the only one outside the commercial vendor world.

What this does not tell you is volume. Five postings is a small sample, and the sources listed include aggregators and remote boards that may not have been fully queried for this function. It also does not show whether these roles are new or backfills, what they pay outside the federal listing, or how the count compares to prior months. Read it as a snapshot of who is hiring for AI education, not as a measure of how much that hiring is growing.
